Select the logical layer. Higher layer order values render above lower ones. The framework assigns actual Canvas orders automatically; these are separate from logical layer order.

Allows this page to become the framework focus owner. The topmost eligible, interactable page takes priority and receives focus notifications. Disabling this does not disable clicks or block input to lower pages.
Enables the modal barrier. None coverage automatically becomes Block Input. Disabling modal removes only automatic blocking; explicitly configured coverage remains in effect.

On back: Close requests closing this page through normal close checks; Ignore continues to lower pages; Block stops the request; Handle by presenter delegates the decision to Presenter. Local back handling inside the page runs first.

None leaves lower pages unchanged. Block input keeps them visible but non-interactable. Hide makes them invisible and non-interactable. This creates no barrier. Lower pages use their own Tick policy to decide whether to pause business updates.

Pause this page’s business Tick when any selected condition is met. Selecting neither disables pausing due to coverage or visibility. This only controls framework business Tick, not Unity Update, animations or coroutines.

Caches only reset Views and their resources after closing, not ViewModels or Presenters. Long-term entries have no time expiry but can still be evicted by capacity or budget limits, or explicit clearing. Reopening reuses a cached View if available; otherwise it creates one. Save and restore business state explicitly.
A full route returns InstanceLimit. Closing the oldest still respects close decisions; returning an existing instance does not update arguments or bring it to front.

Deactivates the selected content subtree when hidden, restoring only content disabled by the framework. Triggers OnDisable/OnEnable and stops subtree coroutines (without resuming them); the View root stays active.

Overrides the gap from this layer’s last page to the next populated layer. -1 uses Default layer gap above; 0 requests no gap; positive values override the default. Empty layers reserve no space. Gaps within a layer are unaffected.

Page order ranges are always enabled. Layers define logical order, not fixed ranges. Root Canvas orders are allocated automatically by page span; compact locally only when space runs out. Maximum + 1 is reserved for closing gesture barriers.
Page gaps apply within a layer; layer gaps apply between layers. They are not added together. Both are measured in orders and shrink when space is tight. Layers do not own fixed ranges.
0 inherits the host default; otherwise at least 2. Offset 0 is the barrier, 1 is the root Canvas; internal Canvas/effects use 2 and above.
Order pool: {0}–{1}; reserved: {2}; page gap: {3}; default layer gap: {4}
Order targets must be unique Canvas/Renderer child references with offsets of at least 2.

Register independent Canvases and all Renderers below. Offsets must be smaller than the page span. Ordinary particles require a camera Canvas and compatible materials; order does not provide UI clipping.

Main pages become current and retire the previous group from presentation. Overlays capture the current main page when requested, or use an explicitly specified page or host owner. Independent views do not participate in main-page navigation.

When the owner leaves the foreground, Close checks permission before closing; Hide and retain restores the overlay on return. Closing the owner closes all its descendants. Closing an overlay does not close its owner.
Backdrop color and opacity. A fully transparent barrier still blocks input. Use transparent tint if a custom blur visual needs no solid color underneath.

Optional visual-only prefab using Image/RawImage and project materials. The project render pipeline supplies blur background textures. Canvas, Renderer, Selectable and View are forbidden. The visual is disabled when hidden; project scripts must release temporary textures.
Unique logical layer name used by page rules. Update references when renaming.
Logical layer priority; larger values appear above smaller ones. Must be unique. This is not a Canvas Order or a fixed range.
Preferred unused Orders between pages in the same logical layer; minimum 0. Reduces reordering and may shrink when space is limited. Cross-layer boundaries use the layer gap instead.
Default unused Orders between populated logical layers; minimum 0. The preceding layer can override this gap. Empty layers reserve nothing; gaps may shrink when space is limited.
Existing Unity Sorting Layer shared by page canvases and registered rendering targets. Separate from logical layers; Orders determine ordering within the host.
Inclusive lower bound of the host Order pool. Must be at least -32768 and below the maximum. Page spans and gaps share this pool.
Inclusive upper bound of the host Order pool; at most 32766. Maximum + 1 is reserved for the release shield. Opening is rejected if reflow cannot provide enough space.

Default number of consecutive Orders per page; minimum 2. Offset 0 is the modal barrier, 1 is the root Canvas, and 2 through span - 1 are for internal canvases/effects. Used when the page span is 0. Gaps are separate.
Used only when ResolvePolicy does not specify a preset. Wizard-generated page entry points explicitly select the preset chosen at creation.
Unique preset name referenced by the default preset and page registrations. Update references when renaming.

Selected groups use this preset’s values; unselected groups inherit page defaults. Instance, cache and timeout settings are overridden as groups. Code-based page overrides can replace individual fields.
Maximum closed Views cached by the host; minimum 0. Zero disables caching. Older entries may be evicted, including KeepAlive entries. Presenters and ViewModels are not cached.
Capacity for pending navigation operations, shared by opens, replacements and argument updates; minimum 1. New requests are rejected at capacity. Not a page instance limit.
Host preload reservation capacity; minimum 1. New preload requests are rejected when reservations reach this limit.
Capacity for instances still exiting or awaiting resource cleanup, including timed-out operations retaining resources; minimum 1. New work is limited at capacity.
Number of completed handle results retained by the host; minimum 1. Older records are removed at capacity. This is neither a View cache nor navigation history.
Allow multiple simultaneous instances of the same route. Otherwise duplicate opens use the existing-instance policy. Multiple instances use the limit and overflow policy.
Maximum instances of the same route; minimum 1. Applies when multiple instances are allowed. The overflow policy handles further opens.
Duplicate single-instance opens either reject or return a ready instance with matching ownership. Reuse does not update arguments or bring the page to the front.
Policy when the route instance limit is reached: reject the request or try to evict an existing instance according to the selected policy. Close guards still apply.
Cache lifetime in seconds; must be positive. Applies only to Timed caching. Expired entries are not reused; capacity pressure may evict them sooner.
Enter transition timeout in seconds; must be positive. Prevents an unfinished enter transition from blocking opening indefinitely.
Exit transition timeout in seconds; must be positive. Prevents an unfinished exit transition from blocking closing indefinitely.
Page preparation timeout in seconds; must be positive. Ends the open wait on timeout; ongoing resource operations remain tracked for cleanup.
Close cleanup timeout in seconds; must be positive. Timeout does not mean resources have been released; unfinished cleanup remains tracked.
Timeout for close guards or user confirmation in seconds; must be positive. Timeout is not treated as approval to close.
When disabled, the page receives no input, does not block UI raycasts, and cannot take focus. Coverage still controls its effect on lower pages.
